gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states measured parking-mode power draw side by side: about 0.43 W for the Viofo A329S in low-power impact detection against 4.98 W (A229 Pro 2CH) and 4.07 W (A229 Plus 2CH) in low-bitrate parking and about 4.1-4.2 W for the Vantrue S1 Pro Max, all measured by named DashCamTalk testers.
standout_why: Compared against thecargearguide's A229 Plus vs A229 Pro vs A329S page (cited), thecargearguide's best front-and-rear page, productbible's best front-and-rear and Viofo-models pages (one cited), pacificpartsdept and roadgearlab. The cited thecargearguide comparison already carries DashCamTalk's measured bitrates (A229 Plus 29/24 Mbps, A229 Pro 57/25, A329S 65/27 front/rear) and its day/night scores, so bitrate is not new. None of the six pages gives a measured watt or mA figure for the A329S, A229 Pro, A229 Plus or any Vantrue in parking or driving mode. thecargearguide's best-of page only relays Vortex Radar's 'under 1mA' (BlackVue Elite 9) and 'up to 40 days' (Thinkware U3000 Pro) and Viofo's own battery-pack figure. Two cited pages could not be read: Car and Driver (fetch refused) and Vortex Radar's best-dashcams page (HTTP 403). Vortex Radar does measure parking current, as its DashCamTalk post shows, so its page may hold part of this; the score of 2 assumes it gives no per-model watt table for the A229 pair and Vantrue.
decides: It confirms the A329S 2CH as the pick for anyone who wants recording while parked, and gives the measured reason. Its low-power impact detection mode draws roughly a tenth of what the A229 Pro 2CH and A229 Plus 2CH draw in their parking modes (0.43 W against 4.98 W and 4.07 W), and wakes in under 3 seconds. The 0.43 W is rcg530's reading on a 3-channel prototype; the only 2-channel figure is Safe Drive Solutions' approximate 39 mA. For a shopper who does not hardwire, it leaves the A229 Pro 2CH value pick unchanged. For our rows: the Vantrue S1 Pro 2CH has a 0.21 W collision-detection mode but takes 12 s to start recording (1.41 W with the 3 s quick start), and 3.88 W in low-bitrate parking. The Vantrue S1 Pro Max draws 8.7 W driving with both cameras and about 4.1-4.2 W in low-bitrate parking, the same range as the A229 Pro 2CH. So on measured parking draw our Vantrue rows match the A229 class in continuous parking recording and trail the A329S's sub-3-second low-power mode.

findings.label: Approximate current draw by channel count (Safe Drive Solutions, 'Ben')
findings.value: 2-channel: 400 mA (5 W) driving, 350 mA low-bitrate parking, 39 mA low power impact detection; 1-channel: 270 mA, 230 mA, 33 mA; 3-channel: 630 mA, 570 mA, 42 mA
findings.source_title: Viofo A329S Review: Tested 4K Footage & Parking Mode (Safe Drive Solutions)
findings.note: Article dated October 7, 2025. This is a retailer review; it calls the figures 'approx.', and states no voltage, instrument or which second camera. Its own 400 mA = 5 W implies 12.5 V; at that voltage 350 mA = 4.4 W and 39 mA = 0.49 W (my arithmetic). Weaker than rcg530, but the only 2-channel figures found.

findings.label: Hours of parked recording on a 96 Wh battery budget (arithmetic from the measured watts)
findings.value: A229 Pro 2CH low bitrate 19.3 h; A229 Plus 2CH low bitrate 23.6 h; Vantrue S1 Pro 2CH low bitrate 24.7 h; Vantrue S1 Pro Max low bitrate about 23 h; A329S low power impact detection about 223 h (9.3 days)
findings.source_title: VIOFO A329S - Testing/Review - RCG, page 11, post #214 by Nigel
findings.note: Nigel (June 6, 2025) suggests 96 Wh, 76 Wh or 57 Wh as car-battery budgets for run-time estimates, depending on the battery life wanted. Arithmetic is mine: 96 / 4.98, 96 / 4.07, 96 / 3.88, 96 / 4.15, 96 / 0.43. The A329S figure is the 3-channel prototype waiting with no impacts; rcg530 calls his own time estimates optimistic. Estimates, not measured run times.
